title: Oil's $116 Target Still Active As Metals Slide
speaker: Drew Dosek (Verified Investing)

macro_themes.view: Gold and silver under pressure from higher yields, breaking supports.
Some de-escalation has pulled oil off its highs but the bullish pattern remains active.

calls.condition: Target stays active only while price holds above the inverse head-and-shoulders neckline; below it the bullish target goes away.
calls.reason: Broken-out inverse head and shoulders with measured move to 116.21; rising parallel support at 88.02 should give a near-term bounce.
calls.quote: as long as price remains above this declining trend line, that targeted measured move is still active

calls.reason: Sep 24 breakout lacked follow-through and price fell back; robust inventories and hedge funds trimming longs; repeated tests weaken support.
calls.quote: likely lead to another push push to the next level lower ... Just a breach of $3 at $2.99

calls.reason: Broke below declining support line under pressure from higher yields; 4104 is the line in the sand, near-term support 3943; also has a head-and-shoulders break.
calls.quote: that is the line in the sand for further downside in the marketplace for gold with the near-term support down here at 3,943

calls.reason: Broken head and shoulders below 61.03 points to ~53.6; around $50 (trend line confluence) he would buy physical silver to hold.
calls.quote: Anything around 50 bucks, I would be a happy buyer

calls.condition: If the bullish consolidation fails, first support 6.33, bigger bounce zone 5.59.
calls.reason: Strong chart with higher lows at top of a parallel channel, but such consolidations usually fail first; expects a dip then a rocket back up as in June.
calls.quote: I'm almost anticipating a similar move. Now, the near-term, it'll be very minor, $6.33

notes: No explicit date; listing used. Garbled prices: '8802'=88.02, '11621'=116.21, '6103'=61.03, '$536'=53.6 (silver), '633'/'559'=6.33/5.59 (copper). Silver 'buy' is for physical silver near $50, not at current price.
